item.title: PBS NewsHour: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to celebrate a milestone with Blue Hippo, Bluey and Megan Moroney
item.description: One of the stars of this year's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade should be very easy to spot. Just look in the sky for a gigantic blue hippo with a goofy smile.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: State Department reports downplay violence and corruption in countries that asylum seekers are fleeing
item.description: The reports use cherry-picked data, careful phrasing and in some cases facts that don't stand up to scrutiny to create misleading depictions of countries that are in fact often plagued by violence, government corruption and police inaction.

item.title: NPR: Group of Senate Democrats push to add freshman to leadership
item.description: Several Democratic senators have been signaling this move, saying the party needs to acknowledge the diverse class of incoming freshman that catapulted the party to victory in November.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Inflation remains stubbornly high, despite a drop in gas prices
item.description: The Commerce Department said Wednesday that consumer prices rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, up from 3.6% in September.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Army offers update after detonating lead azide stockpile in Iowa
item.description: The U.S. Army intentionally blew up the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in southeastern Iowa on Wednesday after officials said the degraded materials were at risk of exploding uncontrollably as temperatures cooled.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration to raise tariffs on China, EU, Brazil and others
item.description: The new tariffs stem from investigations into the trade practices of 12 countries, the 27-member EU and the self-governing island of Taiwan.

item.title: NPR: Republican wants FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia chief
item.description: "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What is lead azide? What to know about the chemical detonated at an Iowa Army base
item.description: The decades-old lead azide supply in Iowa was crystallizing, posing the risk of spontaneous detonation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Live Updates: Army expected to detonate stockpile of lead azide in Iowa
item.description: The U.S. Army plans to detonate the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa around 10 a.m. EST, warning that the degrading bomb-making chemicals could otherwise explode at any time. The controlled detonation of roughly 5 tons (4.54 metric tonnes) of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown has set off concerns about potential health and environmental effects.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Army expected to carry out controlled detonation of Iowa lead azide stockpile
item.description: The controlled detonation of roughly 5 tons of degraded lead azide is planned for 9 a.m. CST at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. It has set off concerns about potential health and environmental impacts from lead dust, and frustration over a lack of information.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: N.C. Democrat reflects on flipping longtime GOP seat: 'It's a new day in the South'
item.description: With most races called, Democrats are on track for a 260-seat majority in the House. No state felt the blue wave more than North Carolina, where Democrats flipped seven House seats and a Senate seat. In the 5th Congressional District, someone never elected to office before, Chuck Hubbard, narrowly beat longtime Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx. Lisa Desjardins spoke with Hubbard about his win.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Thousands of immigrants with legal status lose Medicaid coverage
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of immigrants living legally in the U.S. recently lost their Medicaid coverage under a provision of President Trump's signature tax and spending law. The law is projected to reduce federal Medicaid spending by $900 billion over the next decade. Deema Zein reports on what that loss of coverage means for some of those affected.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bob Woodward reveals why he's naming sources in new book 'Secrets'
item.description: For over five decades, veteran journalist Bob Woodward has exposed some of Washington's closely kept secrets. In his new memoir fittingly titled "Secrets," he lets us in on some of his own, and unmasks the anonymous sources that allowed him incredible access to ten American presidents. Amna Nawaz sat down with Woodward and discussed why he chose to name some of them now.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'Deals Drama Drive' traces how the Mondavi family helped spark Napa Valley's wine boom
item.description: In 1966, Robert Mondavi and his son Michael opened Robert Mondavi Winery in California's Napa Valley. There, father and son helped spark a revolution and transform the region into one of the world's premier winemaking destinations. A new biography, "Deals Drama Drive: Michael Mondavi and the making of Napa Valley," tells the story. Michael Mondavi joined Geoff Bennett to discuss more.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How Trump may have profited from Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description: A day after President Trump intervened to reinstate Nvidia's embattled CEO, a new report suggests that Trump himself may have benefited financially to the tune of millions of dollars. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What's next for Nvidia and Jensen Huang after Trump's intervention
item.description: Questions are still being raised about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO, the role President Trump played in that decision and what other investigations could mean for the company. To help break it all down, Amna Nawaz spoke with Greg Ip, chief economics commentator for The Wall Street Journal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: California's king tides could be biggest in 4 decades
item.description: In our news wrap Tuesday, California is bracing for king tides along the Pacific coast that could be the biggest in four decades, President Trump awarded Rudolph Giuliani the Medal of Freedom, FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia is reportedly retiring in December and a jury in New York found Chinese tech giant Huawei guilty of conspiring to steal U.S. trade secrets and evading sanctions.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Army plans explosive detonation in Iowa despite residents' concerns
item.description: The U.S. Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate a highly volatile explosive compound in Iowa. The lead azide is used in military munitions and has been deteriorating underground. The detonation could send a plume of toxic lead dust across the area, but Army officials insist a controlled explosion is the safest option. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Eliza Billingham of Iowa Public Radio.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: States sue HUD over a rule that would end housing aid for mixed-status families
item.description: HUD defends the rule, saying it prevents illegal immigrants from exploiting eligibility requirements.
item.category: Department of Housing and Urban Development

item.title: NPR: Moving to Florida may become a choice of some Republicans after midterms
item.description: In Florida, Republicans kept power of state government after the midterms. It's now the largest state where the GOP is still in charge.

item.title: NPR: Ex-White House AI adviser weighs in on national security as Huang is back as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back in leadership after resigning recently. Ben Buchanan, a Biden administration AI adviser, discusses what that means for U.S. national security and chip exports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Paxton drops Texas lawsuits that accused doctors of illegally providing transgender youth care
item.description: May Lau and M. Brett Cooper were among three doctors who Paxton called "scofflaws" and "radical gender activists" in lawsuits that threatened to impose steep fines and revoke their medical licenses.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. jury finds Chinese tech giant Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud
item.description: Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries under U.S. sanctions and making false statements to officials.

item.title: NPR: The U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels
item.description: The attacks, if officials who spoke to NPR are correct, may be the latest example of Iranian cyberattacks against global critical infrastructure during the war with the U.S.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pentagon sharply criticizes Canada over modernizing military
item.description: The Defense Department accused Ottawa of failing to make the tough decisions needed to modernize its military and meet NATO commitments.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Australia set to pass online safety laws with multibillion-dollar fines for tech giants
item.description: The Australian government clinched a political deal on Tuesday to introduce online safety laws that could expose tech giants to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats supporting abortion rights won big in midterms, but vast changes unlikely soon
item.description: States with bans will still have enough Republicans in power to likely block any repeal attempts for now.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Chinese neuroscientist at Princeton held by ICE after detention at D.C. airport
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security says Xie overstayed her visa and did not have authorization to study in the U.S. Xie's lawyer says she has a pending asylum application.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Experts say failed climate talks could worsen inequality, but progress not stalled
item.description: Dozens of nations objected to the summit's final text because it didn't mention fossil fuels that drive climate change or increase financial help for poorer countries.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: West Coast king tides could break decades-old records and flood communities
item.description: In the San Francisco Bay Area, tides could reach 2.6 feet above normal Tuesday before peaking Wednesday at 2.8 feet above normal, said Dial Hoang, a National Weather Service forecaster.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Will wind ground your favorite balloon in Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade?
item.description: Local officials are wary of the balloons getting blown off course and into spectators. Macy's says it'll make the decision Thursday morning.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump will give Medal of Freedom to Giuliani, a fierce political ally who led New York through 9/11
item.description: As President Donald Trump's personal lawyer, he was a central figure in efforts to overturn Trump's 2020 presidential election loss to Democrat Joe Biden.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Rep. Raskin expands investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s investment firm
item.description: A top House Democrat is broadening his investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s venture capital fund 1789 Capital by demanding records from four companies that secured an investment before benefiting from lucrative federal contracts or policies.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 2 men arrested over suspected burglary at Prince William and Kate's country home
item.description: Police said that "the property was unoccupied at the time of the incident."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump's intervention on behalf of Jensen Huang gives Democrats more 2028 campaign fuel
item.description: Still euphoric over their sweeping midterm victories, many ambitious Democrats are still feeling around for the right message on artificial intelligence, which carries both promise and peril as it becomes increasingly intertwined with the economy, infrastructure and daily life.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Records show how DOJ, judge debated constitutional implications of searching Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
item.description: The unsealed filings show that U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh — before authorizing the search of Omar's home — raised concerns about the "Speech or Debate Clause" implications of searching a private residence belonging to a member of Congress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Francis' private diary reveals pope grappling with spiritual crisis and encounters with the devil
item.description: Pope Francis saw the "gates of hell" when he realized the depths of the clergy sexual abuse scandal and experienced mystical visions of the devil throughout his ministry, according to excerpts of his personal diary published Tuesday by the Vatican.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back on top at Nvidia
item.description: The president has staked the nation's economic growth on artificial intelligence.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump holds 2026 White House turkey pardon with Freedom and Feathers
item.description: Both birds will get a reprieve from ending up on a Thanksgiving dinner table, but only one of them will get a ceremonial pardon at the White House.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Getting court approval, U.S. Army to detonate degraded bomb-making material in Iowa on Wednesday
item.description: The detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide was initially planned for last Friday, but the Army has since changed the date three times following an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.

item.title: NPR: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia. And, Rep. Gomez resigns amid alleged sexual misconduct
item.description: President Trump took credit for negotiating Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. And, Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.

item.title: NPR: Trump takes credit for Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, says its good for the economy
item.description: President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company -- and good for the United States economy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Millions of Americans have medical debt. Experts worry the problem is about to get worse
item.description: Medical debt is increasingly a risk for people with health insurance, experts say.

item.title: NPR: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
item.description: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.

item.title: NPR: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
item.description: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why Trump pushed for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia just two weeks after resigning amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. President Trump personally intervened to push for his reinstatement, saying he believed Huang did nothing wrong. White House correspondent Liz Landers spoke with President Trump before the announcement.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Experts weigh national security implications of Huang's return to Nvidia
item.description: For a closer look at Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, and the national security implications, Amna Nawaz spoke with Dmitri Alperovitch and James Lewis. Alperovitch co-founded and was chief technology officer of the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike. Lewis is a former diplomat with extensive intelligence experience. He's now with the Tech Policy Program at the Center for European Policy Analysis.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Storms threaten Thanksgiving travel as airlines rebound from tech failures
item.description: In our news wrap Monday, storms on both coasts threaten to disrupt Thanksgiving travel as airlines continue to grapple with a series of recent tech failures, a federal appeals court says the Army can proceed with detonating bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunitions plant and Ukraine says it struck a Russian warship docked in Libya.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Seattle airport arrests renew protests over ICE enforcement tactics
item.description: New questions are being raised about ICE's training and enforcement tactics after officers arrested a father and daughter as they were boarding a flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The incident comes as The New York Times reports new findings from the Department of Homeland Security's inspector general. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Hamed Aleaziz of The New York Times.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Severe drought pushes millions in Afghanistan deeper into crisis
item.description: Afghanistan is in the throes of a severe economic crisis. Last year, nearly three-quarters of the population was living in poverty, according to the United Nations. Now, millions of Afghans are facing drought and have no access to safe drinking water. Special correspondent Leila Molana-Allen and videographer Eric O'Connor traveled to the Bamyan province, one of the country's poorest regions.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tamara Keith and Amy Walter on Trump's role in Huang's reinstatement
item.description: NPR's Tamara Keith and Amy Walter of the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter join Amna Nawaz to discuss the latest political news, including President Trump taking credit for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, how Democrats will operate with large margins in the House and Senate, the government funding deadline and their favorite Thanksgiving dish.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The science of how pets see and respond to screens
item.description: Have you ever been sitting on your couch, watching a TV show, and noticed your dog is paying attention to the screen? A recent social media trend has raised new questions about how our canine friends engage with shows and movies. William Brangham reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What's driving up the cost of Thanksgiving dinner
item.description: As we approach Thanksgiving, Americans are heading to the grocery store ahead of the traditional meal with family and friends. But how much will that turkey and the fixings cost you this year? Digital reporter Tim McPhillips breaks down the numbers.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What military families see as their biggest challenges as Trump's new military spouse commission convenes
item.description: Military spouses interviewed by PBS News say there is more to do to improve quality of life for military families.

item.title: NPR: California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
item.description: California Congressman Rep. Jimmy Gomez says he will resign after a House Ethics report concluded Gomez's actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ethics probe finds Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez made unwelcome sexual advances to a staffer
item.description: The House Ethics Committee said in a report released Monday that there is "substantial evidence" that Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez of California engaged in sexual misconduct by making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a House staffer.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia sparks fury in Congress as lawmakers move forward with hearings
item.description: Nvidia was already facing sharp scrutiny from Congress after Huang acknowledged a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. officials believed to be a spy. Putting Huang back in charge, after Trump said the board did "what we wanted them to do," raised stark concerns over the administration's role in the company that is central to the AI economy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump told the Army to pause the detonation of 9,500 pounds of lead azide in Iowa. Here's what to know
item.description: The U.S. Army's controlled detonation of 68 barrels of unstable lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday is expected to produce a plume of dust containing lead particles that could extend as far as 100 miles away, a plan that residents, lawmakers and environmental groups say was not communicated appropriately.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump a path to erasing hush money conviction
item.description: The decision moves the case to a federal court, where Trump could seek to have charges dismissed on immunity grounds.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Airline glitches and storms could make Thanksgiving travel messy
item.description: A cascade of technical glitches that have upended airlines over the past week are adding to the unease.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump says Army will not detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa without court approval
item.description: President Donald Trump says he will defer to a federal appeals court on whether to proceed with detonating degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Senate leadership vote tests newly elected Democrats' promise of change
item.description: The Democratic Party's incoming senators face an early test of their campaign promises to shake up Washington as they decide who will lead their new majority.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump delivers address on Newsom's move to grant clemency for California's death row
item.description: The White House said the speech would be about protecting American families and Newsom's decision to commute the death sentences of more than 500 inmates to punishments of life without parole.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Writers unhappy with PEN America's response to war in Gaza form new chapter
item.description: Novelist Maaza Mengiste says they don't seek rivalry with PEN America but differ in structure and priorities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Some sheriffs who signed pacts to help Trump's immigration enforcement efforts ousted by voters
item.description: Trump has encouraged local law enforcement agencies to sign partnerships with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. More than 2,700 agreements are in place nationwide.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. to co-host 2031 Women's World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica
item.description: The UK, led by England, will host the 2035 edition.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The collapse of UN climate talks over fossil fuels was years in the making
item.description: While negotiations collapsed over one main point of contention — whether to include language about fossil fuels, the main driver of global warming — this fight over this has been building for many years.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Medicare for All was once a long shot. Now universal healthcare is on the Democrats' agenda
item.description: The details are still taking shape, and there will almost certainly be pushback from moderate and centrist Democrats.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Trump told PBS News about Jensen Huang before Nvidia reinstatement
item.description: In a phone call with PBS News shortly after 8 a.m. EST Monday, Trump did not deny that he had been briefed, saying he was "not going to comment on anything having to do with that. You'll have to figure that out for yourself."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats plan 12 debates for their 2028 presidential primary, with what's likely to be a crowded field
item.description: The debates could be play a key role in generating attention for what is expected to be a broad field of candidates vying to succeed Republican President Donald Trump.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from Don Toliver concert after an unknown substance sickens fans
item.description: One person was hospitalized, and more than 50 were assessed for eye and respiratory symptoms.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
item.description: Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman
item.description: In a statement Monday, the board said it "believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How a billionaire tax proposal failed in California despite big election wins for progressives
item.description: In an election with major wins for Democrats and progressives nationwide, California voters not only rejected the biggest test yet for a state wealth tax, they also approved a measure making it much harder to enact one in the future.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'One of the very worst.' Jan. 6 leader Stewart Rhodes says he is 'absolutely done' with Trump
item.description: "We elected him to end the corruption in Washington, D.C. 'Drain the swamp.' Unfortunately his administration has been one of the most corrupt administrations in U.S. history," Rhodes said.

item.title: NPR: Democrats win House by largest margin in 50 years. And, COP31 ends with no deal
item.description: Democrats have currently flipped 47 House seats and could flip 49 total. And, climate change talks at COP31 ran two days longer than expected, becoming the longest conference in the summit's history.

item.title: NPR: After midterm losses, Republicans debate what's next for the party
item.description: In the wake of their midterm election losses, Republicans are discussing what happened and what the future might be for their party.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Lawyer: Father and daughter detained by ICE at Seattle airport were traveling to family baptism
item.description: Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: In their own words: Leaders at UN climate talks discuss why negotiations ended without deal
item.description: After reviewing a draft of the agreement released by co-host Turkey, a number of countries spoke up during the final meeting Sunday to say they couldn't accept a deal that failed to include wording on fossil fuels.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Automation system problem at Delta causes flight delays as Americans travel for Thanksgiving
item.description: Earlier Sunday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued about an hourlong ground stop to some flights into Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is Delta's hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Today's Thanksgiving holiday was invented amid the Civil War to unite a divided country
item.description: The idea of a straight line connecting that "first Thanksgiving" to Thanksgivings today is, in fact, an American myth.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Appeals court says federal law requiring accommodations for pregnant workers is unconstitutional
item.description: The appeals court said the act was unconstitutional because a majority of U.S. House members weren't physically present when it was approved as part of a spending package in December 2022.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. Army plans to invoke emergency provisions to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
item.description: Environmental groups criticized the government's move, decrying it as a maneuver to get around a court order and avoid public demands for safety and transparency.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Poland says Russia allegedly twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper
item.description: Denmark is expected to ask the European Union this week for more decisive action stemming from the case, perhaps restricting Russian citizens from entering and traveling freely within the EU. Poland said it would support such measures.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. intelligence chief says Trump's description of Putin as a 'friend' is 'entirely appropriate'
item.description: Clayton defended comments that Democrats have characterized as a betrayal of American values after Trump met with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping for rare three-way talks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats, the largest since 1992
item.description: The 258-seat tally was reached Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Scientists are fighting for their halted funds. Trust of Black communities may be harder to win back
item.description: The study was among broader research into why Black Americans are twice as likely as their white peers to develop Alzheimer's, but the Trump administration abruptly halted it in its final stretch.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: French activists demand a tear gas suspension over reported menstrual changes
item.description: Some women reported painful cramps, unexpected bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after exposure, and an advocacy group says it has collected more than 10,000 complaints.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: As AI detects flaws in computer systems, is it causing more tech outages and disruptions?
item.description: AI rapidly identifies computer system vulnerabilities and companies are pressured to fix them. Experts say that might lead to unintended consequences, like tech outages.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
item.description: BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury — the sun's closest planet and barely bigger than our moon — and the first in more than a decade.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UN climate talks break down over bitter disagreements on fossil fuels
item.description: Expectations had already been low heading into the two-week negotiations in Turkey, but impasses over explicitly including fossil fuels and other issues, including money, proved irreconcilable.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Immigration officers make arrests at Seattle airport in 'distressing' scene, delaying flight
item.description: Video of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as a woman screams that her daughter is being taken and she has a work permit.

item.title: NPR: Politics chat: Lawmakers step up with only weeks to Democrats' control of Congress
item.description: A funding deadline for Congress weeks before Democrats take control. President Trump signs an executive order requiring contractors to get approval before sharing with Congressional investigations.

item.title: NPR: Christian nationalist conference hosts Nick Fuentes, vows to keep pushing MAGA agenda
item.description: A particular group of Christian nationalists met in Texas last weekend and vowed to push what remains of MAGA as far to the right as possible. They hosted antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes.

item.title: NPR: It's Medicare open enrollment time. Here's what you need to know
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Why do people believe recent tech failures must be connected?
item.description: Even without clear evidence, people drew connections between recent tech failures and outages. The way our brains and social media platforms work helps explain why.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: For families of the fallen, Trump's proposed arch casts a shadow over Arlington National Cemetery
item.description: Trump's proposed 250-foot-tall arch could cast a long shadow on Arlington National Cemetery, with the potential to literally shade gravesites, disrupt solemn visits with the noise of construction and alter the carefully designed historic landscape of the nation's capital.

item.title: NPR: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
item.description: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%
item.description: The standard proposal would substantially reduce what credit card companies can charge customers. The median credit card interest rate is roughly 22.2%, according to an August survey by the New York Federal Reserve.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP source: FBI investigating apparent hack of its key national criminal justice database
item.description: The National Crime Information Center, known as the NCIC, is a computerized database of criminal justice information that is available to local, state and federal law enforcement agencies and includes records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history data, stolen property and other topics.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A doctor's guide to surviving — and enjoying — holiday feasting while on GLP‑1 medication
item.description: Changes in appetite, smaller portion tolerance, limits on alcohol consumption, medication side effects and the desire to maintain progress can make navigating holiday traditions feel a little different.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
item.description: The order is the Republican administration's latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off a burst of violence in Sinaloa
item.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives. He climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump auditions potential successors as Rubio and Vance join him for White House briefing
item.description: It was the latest episode in the public audition that the president and former reality television star has appeared to delight in arranging for his potential successors as he nears his last two years in office.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Climate talks in overtime as nations wrestle with response to worsening global warming
item.description: The added day of talks came as the two-week annual summit, or COP31, drew strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Texas says an execution went as planned. A witness says screams showed 'tremendous distress'
item.description: Executions across the U.S. have garnered more attention since Christa Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital in Tennessee in September. The drug didn't enter her bloodstream correctly.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bessent says no further restrictions are needed for Nvidia chip exports to China
item.description: "The proper chip restrictions are in place," Bessent said in an interview with CNBC after returning from a trip to Asia with President Donald Trump. "And the remote access has been curtailed."

item.title: NPR: How a GOP redistricting 'dummymander' in North Carolina backfired by 2 seats
item.description: In North Carolina, Republican lawmakers redrew voting maps, aiming to gain one seat in Congress. Instead, they lost two seats, in a classic example of what political scientists call a "dummymander."

item.title: NPR: The New Yorker's Jason Zengerle on Hakeem Jeffries' rise to first Black House speaker
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first-ever African American speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Jason Zengerle of The New Yorker about the rise of Jeffries.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Trump returns from Asia; hails trip as one of best in history
item.description: President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent -- or anywhere else -- in American history.

item.title: NPR: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
item.description: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Rights groups urge sanctions after ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice has no power to enforce Thursday's ruling, which orders Myanmar's military-supported government to allow those who fled the violence to return home safely, to pay reparations to the Rohingya Muslims and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Federal jury convicts man of starting deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
item.description: The man accused of sparking last year's deadly Palisades Fire was found guilty of arson charges Friday after his first federal case earlier this year ended in a mistrial.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Trump addressed during his lengthy White House news conference
item.description: In a lengthy press conference, President Trump touted his recent trip to Asia and defended his relationship with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. White House correspondent Liz Landers was in the briefing room as the president took questions from reporters.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Stocks tumble as worries about AI rattle market
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, stocks tumbled to end the week as worries about AI rattled the market, a second federal judge is blocking President Trump's triumphal arch in Washington and a federal appeals court is blocking the Army from detonating several tons of bomb-making chemicals amid concerns over environmental and health risks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mounting tech disruptions raise concerns about U.S. cybersecurity
item.description: President Trump has replaced the nation's top cybersecurity official following a string of seemingly unrelated technology outages over the last couple of weeks. Officials have repeatedly stressed that these outages were not the result of intentional attacks, but given the growth of AI, there's growing concern that attacks are on the horizon. William Brangham discussed more with Chris Krebs.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Josh Shapiro on foreign policy, Democratic wins and his 2028 ambitions
item.description: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro is fresh off a reelection campaign that gave him another four years in office and Democrats majorities in the state House. Now Shapiro is turning his attention to foreign policy, laying out his prescriptions to solve pressing global crises. Amna Nawaz sat down with the governor to discuss his vision for how the United States should engage on the world stage.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Fiona's caretakers and fans mourn the beloved hippo after her death at Cincinnati Zoo
item.description: Born prematurely almost a decade ago and given slim odds of survival, Fiona became not only a source of hometown pride but also a worldwide symbol of hope and inspiration for many.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's summit with Putin and Xi
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including President Trump's trilateral summit with Xi and Putin, the ongoing debate surrounding data centers, and Elon Musk's attempt to distance himself from MAGA.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Inside the museum preserving the story of JFK's assassination
item.description: On November 22, 1963, President John F. Kennedy was killed while driving in a motorcade in downtown Dallas. As the story continues to be told and questioned, those memories are preserved and displayed at The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown visited the museum for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Court approves $7.25 billion Bayer settlement over claims Roundup weed killer caused cancer
item.description: Agrochemical maker Bayer will pay up to $7.25 billion over two decades to resolve thousands of claims from U.S. cancer patients asserting the company should have warned people that its popular weed killer Roundup could cause lymphoma, according to a settlement approved Friday by a Missouri judge.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Activists, leaders criticize COP31 climate talks as fossil fuels go unmentioned in draft deal
item.description: United Nations climate talks in Turkey stretched into overtime Friday and delegates put off some decisions to next year, unable to find common ground on multiple issues with mutterings and protests about failure.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Lawsuits allege corner cutting, ignored warnings led to fatal Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: As investigators probe what caused a New York City building collapse that killed eight people, workers and residents are painting a portrait of two trouble spots side-by-side: the apartment house that fell down and the construction site being excavated next door.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: NATO calls Russian missiles landing in Poland a 'grave violation' of airspace
item.description: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.

item.title: NPR: The latest from Trump's press conference
item.description: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Second federal judge blocks construction of Trump's memorial arch
item.description: A second federal judge has blocked President Donald Trump's administration from building a 250-foot memorial arch in the nation's capital, issuing an order on Friday that keeps the construction work on hold indefinitely, according to plaintiffs' lawyers who sued to challenge the project.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump on data centers: 'Take advantage, don't shut them off'
item.description: The president said he doesn't want to allow the centers to be built outside the U.S. "because China will take all of them." He added that companies that try to build elsewhere will face "tremendous penalties."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Cascade of tech outages 'separate events' and 'under control,' Trump says
item.description: "If there's any silver lining to what happened last week, it's that Congress seems to be very receptive now to giving us the money," Trump said about the administration's plan to overhaul air traffic control.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump says he would love former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to 'be given a second chance'
item.description: "We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them," Trump said during a press conference at the White House, touting Nvidia as "a very important company to us."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: 'We will not allow that to happen,' Trump says of reported Iran dirty bomb threat
item.description: "We know a lot about what's happening in Iran," Trump said, speaking during a press briefing at the White House. "We know everything they say. We know who they are, where they are. We'll find out about it."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Court grants request to prevent military from detonating bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
item.description: The detonation was initially planned for Friday, but the Army pushed it to Monday following an outpouring of public concern about the potential health and environmental consequences.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump defends calling Putin a friend, saying they have a 'very good' personal relationship
item.description: The Republican president appeared to sidestep a question about whether he sees Putin as a friend to the United States.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Northeastern Florida now under flood threats from heavy rain that has devastated coastal communities
item.description: Parts of Florida's east coast have been deluged with rainfall totaling more than 17 inches in some spots since Tuesday, according to preliminary totals by the weather service.

item.title: NPR: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
item.description: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Travelers' concerns spike as Thanksgiving nears and tech hiccups grow, but few are dissuaded
item.description: Just like bad weather, air travel disruptions irritate many Americans while dissuading comparatively few.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mamdani sets plan to close NYC's notorious Rikers Island jail by 2032
item.description: The mayor unveiled the plan as the city is all but certain to blow past a legal requirement to close Rikers and replace it with four smaller, more modern jails by 2027.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sales of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' hit more than $2.3 billion after long-anticipated release
item.description: The game, which launched on Thursday, has hit $2.36 billion in revenue with approximately 24.6 million units sold.

item.title: NPR: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
item.description: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump hosts news conference after meeting with Xi, Putin
item.description: Trump's meeting on Thursday was the first-ever sit-down for the leaders of the U.S., Russia and China.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Myanmar is the first state found responsible for genocide. Here's how the ICJ ruled in other cases
item.description: The International Court of Justice has been asked to reach that conclusion before, but never found enough evidence to make the determination of a state-sponsored genocide like the one targeting the Rohingya.

item.title: NPR: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war
item.description: "We're not going to shut down the war," Sen. Ron Johnson said as Republicans and Democrats struggle to reach a government funding deal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Iran war has permanently reshaped energy priorities, IEA report says
item.description: The repercussions from the Iran war will "leave lasting marks" on the world's energy sector, said the Paris-based IEA, founded after the 1973-74 oil crisis.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: U.S. Capitol Christmas tree arrives in D.C.
item.description: Placing a tree outside the Capitol building has been a tradition for more than 60 years.

item.title: NPR: Trump to hold press conference after meeting with Xi and Putin
item.description: Trump did not formally take questions while in China at the end of his trip, though it's typically expected on presidential foreign trips.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration moves to have lawsuit dismissed in challenge to Alaska's U.S. Senate race
item.description: In their filing, Justice Department attorneys urged the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to overturn the lower court's dismissal of the case to erase the loss, but then dismiss the case anyway.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: White House taps Kirsten Davies as cyber chief after outages rattle Americans
item.description: The White House named a new national cyber director Thursday after a series of widespread service outages disrupted life and unnerved many Americans.

item.title: NPR: Texas execution took over an hour as staff struggled to find vein; Reinaldo Dennes moaned about pain
item.description: The same day Dennes was given lethal injection, Florida carried out a record-breaking 20th execution of the year.

item.title: NPR: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa
item.description: Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

item.title: NPR: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
item.description: As Americans struggle with rising energy costs and increased demand driven by AI, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that will speed up the approval process for data centers and power plants.

item.title: NPR: New York City unveils a bold plan to move its jails off Rikers Island
item.description: New York City officials are moving forward with plans to close Rikers, the city's main jail complex, after years of discussion. The jail has been plagued by assaults and inmate deaths.
